ai.literal: Lack of knowledge among poverties [is] poverty; lack of other things, as poverty does not consider the world.
ai.translation: The ultimate poverty is the lack of knowledge. The world does not consider the lack of other things to be poverty at all.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாமல் இருப்பதே வறுமைகளுள் எல்லாம் கொடிய வறுமையாகும். மற்ற செல்வங்கள் இல்லாதிருப்பதை உலகம் ஒரு வறுமையாகக் கருதாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts intellectual poverty with material poverty. The word 'இன்மை' (iṉmai) is used repeatedly to mean both 'lack' and 'poverty'. The text states that being without knowledge is the worst kind of destitution among all poverties. In contrast, lacking 'other things' (பிறிது), which implies material wealth, is not even considered true poverty by the world.

ai.literal: One without knowledge heart having rejoiced giving, other anything is not, receiver's penance.
ai.translation: When a fool gives with a joyful heart, it is due to nothing else but the penance of the receiver.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவன் மனம் மகிழ்ந்து ஒரு பொருளைக் கொடுத்தால், அதற்குக் காரணம் வேறொன்றும் இல்லை; பொருளைப் பெறுகின்றவன் செய்த தவமே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the rare event of a foolish person giving generously. Since a fool lacks the wisdom to understand the value of charity, their joyful giving is not a result of their own virtue. Instead, it is entirely the result of the good deeds or penance (தவம்) previously performed by the person who receives the gift. The phrase 'பிறிதியாதும் இல்லை' emphasizes that there is absolutely no other reason for this unexpected generosity.

ai.literal: Knowledge those-without, they themselves themselves which-afflict suffering, to-enemies-even doing is-difficult.
ai.translation: The suffering that the ignorant inflict upon themselves is hard even for their enemies to cause.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்கள் தங்களுக்குத் தாங்களே உண்டாக்கிக் கொள்ளும் துன்பத்தை, அவர்களுடைய பகைவர்களாலும் அவர்களுக்குச் செய்வது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the self-destructive nature of ignorance. The phrase 'அறிவு இலார்' refers to those lacking wisdom or proper understanding. Because of their foolish actions, they bring 'பீழை' (suffering) upon themselves. The poet emphasizes the severity of this self-inflicted harm by stating that even their worst enemies ('செறுவார்க்கும்') would find it difficult to cause them such immense pain. Thus, ignorance is portrayed as a person's greatest enemy.

ai.literal: Ignorance that which is called if asked what it is, wisdom we possess we saying conceit.
ai.translation: If asked what is called true ignorance, it is the conceit of proudly declaring, 'We possess wisdom.'
ai.modern: அறியாமை என்று சொல்லப்படுவது எது என்றால், 'நாம் மிகுந்த அறிவுடையோம்' என்று தமக்குத் தாமே நினைத்துக்கொள்ளும் செருக்குதான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essence of ignorance or folly. The word 'veṇmai' literally means whiteness or emptiness, but here it signifies a blank, ignorant mind. True ignorance is not merely a lack of knowledge, but the arrogant conceit ('cerukku') of believing and declaring that one is already wise ('oṇmai'). Such false pride prevents a person from ever acquiring real wisdom.

ai.literal: Unlearned having undertaken behaving flaw to be removed even that which is mastered doubt will yield
ai.translation: Pretending to possess knowledge one has not learned will cast doubt even upon the subjects one has mastered flawlessly.
ai.modern: படிக்காதவற்றைப் படித்ததாகக் காட்டிக்கொண்டு நடப்பது, ஒருவன் குற்றமறக் கற்று வல்லமையாக உள்ளவற்றின் மீதும் மற்றவர்களுக்குச் சந்தேகத்தை ஏற்படுத்தும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the pretense of knowledge. When an ignorant person pretends to know things they have not actually learned, their behavior exposes their deceit. Consequently, others will begin to doubt even the genuine skills and knowledge that the person has mastered flawlessly. The word 'வல்லதூஉம்' uses a poetic elongation to emphasize that absolutely everything they are truly capable of becomes suspect.

ai.literal: Nakedness covering? Folly, in oneself fault not-covering when.
ai.translation: What is the use of covering one's physical nakedness? It is mere folly, when one fails to cover the faults within oneself.
ai.modern: தன்னிடம் உள்ள குற்றங்களை நீக்கி மறைக்காத போது, உடலின் மறைவிடங்களை மட்டும் ஆடையால் மறைப்பது அறியாமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts physical modesty with moral modesty. The word 'அற்றம்' refers to physical nakedness, while 'குற்றம்' refers to moral flaws. The poet points out the hypocrisy of covering one's body with clothes while leaving one's inner faults exposed and uncorrected. Maintaining outward decency without hiding and curing one's own flaws is sheer folly.

ai.literal: Rare secret lets slip wisdom he-who-lacks does great harm himself to himself.
ai.translation: The ignorant man who lets slip precious secrets brings great harm upon himself by his own doing.
ai.modern: அரிய ரகசியங்களை வாய்தவறி வெளிப்படுத்தும் அறிவில்லாதவன், தனக்குத் தானே பெரிய துன்பத்தை உண்டாக்கிக் கொள்வான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the self-destructive nature of an ignorant person. The phrase 'அருமறை சோரும்' refers to carelessly letting slip precious or important secrets. By failing to guard such secrets, the foolish person ('அறிவிலான்') brings about severe harm ('பெருமிறை') upon himself. The words 'தானே தனக்கு' emphasize that he is the sole author of his own downfall, needing no enemies to ruin him.

ai.literal: Even when commanded he does not do, himself he does not understand; that life until it goes is a disease.
ai.translation: A person who neither does what he is told nor understands what to do himself is a disease until his life departs.
ai.modern: சொன்னாலும் செய்யமாட்டான், தானாகவும் எதையும் சிந்தித்து அறியமாட்டான்; அப்படிப்பட்டவனுடைய உயிர் அவன் உடலை விட்டுப் போகும் வரைக்கும் உலகத்திற்கு ஒரு நோயாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the ultimate frustration of dealing with a foolish person. The word 'ஏவவும்' means even when explicitly instructed, while 'தான் தேறான்' means he lacks the capacity to figure things out on his own. The poet concludes that such a 'life' (உயிர்) is merely a 'disease' (நோய்) to society, offering no value until the day it finally departs (போஒம் அளவும்).

ai.literal: He who does not see, he who shows, himself will not see; he who does not see, he who has seen becomes, the way he himself has seen.
ai.translation: He who tries to teach a man who cannot see will himself fail to see. The man who cannot see will think he has seen, but only in his own limited way.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவனுக்கு அறிவுரை கூற முயல்பவன், தானும் அறிவில்லாதவன் ஆவான். அந்த அறிவில்லாதவனோ, தனக்குத் தெரிந்த அளவிலேயே தான் எல்லாம் அறிந்தவனாக நினைத்துக்கொள்வான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the futility of trying to teach someone who is stubbornly ignorant. The word 'காணாதான்' refers to a person who lacks understanding or refuses to see the truth. If a wise person tries to show ('காட்டுவான்') the truth to such a person, the wise person's efforts will fail, making him look foolish ('தான் காணான்'). Furthermore, the ignorant person will simply twist the teaching to fit his own flawed perspective ('தான் கண்ட ஆறு'), falsely believing he has understood everything ('கண்டானாம்').

ai.literal: people of the world / exists / that which is said / does not exist / he who says / in the world / as a demon / to be placed / will be
ai.translation: He who denies what the people of the world affirm to exist, will be considered a demon on earth.
ai.modern: உலகத்து உயர்ந்தோர் உண்டு என்று சொல்வதை இல்லை என்று மறுப்பவன், இந்த உலகத்தில் ஒரு பேயாகவே கருதப்படுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the extreme folly of denying universal truths. When a person stubbornly rejects what the wise people of the world ('உலகத்தார்') collectively affirm to exist ('உண்டு என்பது'), he isolates himself from human reason. Because of this unnatural and destructive mindset, he is not seen as a normal human being but is classified as a demon ('அலகையா') wandering the earth. The word 'அலகை' (demon or ghost) emphasizes his alienation from human society and common sense.
